result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever the rest of the name is. That covers plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`. The existing `ScopingConventions*` tests pass. I didn't add new test cases or run the new patterns against the example paths.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394), I changed the two patterns from `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` to `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`.

- **Scope of the match:** the rule needs a `/` right before `mock`, so it stays inside a single folder name. `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` are not matched.
- **Windows paths:** `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already also tries each path with backslashes converted to `/`, so those work without further changes.
- **Folders classified as test before:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match, since `[^/]*` accepts everything the old character class did.

I didn't commit.
